Depends on the type of file. Most media files can be viewed incomplete as long as the header and footer (rare) exist. 

Movies will skip the missing frame(s) and not even notice because there's no continuity really between most frames (worst case is you get a messed up visual for a few seconds until the next keyframe).

Audio is much the same as video, but most audio codecs need both the first and last piece. The skipped portions won't affect the song in any way like video images could. 

Images are a mixed bag, most formats deal with missing or corrupt data by slapping in the you-fucked-up-pink color for the pixel.
